bug: LIKE or GLOB pattern too complex (D1 SQLITE_ERROR, code 7500)
rootCause: D1 (Cloudflare's HTTP-hosted SQLite) rejects any LIKE/GLOB pattern whose total string length (including the '%' wildcards) exceeds ~50 characters. This is an undocumented platform limit, empirically measured via binary search against the real D1 database (40/42/44/46/48 chars of content = OK; 50/52/54/56/58/60/62 = FAIL). node:sqlite locally does NOT reproduce this even at 10,000 chars — it is D1-specific, not a general SQLite limitation.
triggerCondition: A search query long enough that '%' + query + '%' exceeds 50 chars. TBCA-derived food names are frequently 90-150+ characters when normalized (e.g. long composite-dish descriptions), so any code path that builds a LIKE pattern directly from a full free-text food query was exposed.

callSitesFound.role: PRIMARY cause — runs on every single food search (CUSTOM/MANUFACTURER are always in the default source filter), so any long query broke the search before even reaching the USDA fallback.
SECONDARY — only hit when the local (TACO/CUSTOM) catalog returns fewer than LOCAL_RESULTS_SUFFICIENT_FOR_USDA candidates, or USDA is explicitly requested.
LATENT — the LIKE fallback only runs when FTS is unavailable; never actually triggered in the real shadow runs, fixed preventively.

MISSED IN THE FIRST PASS — the actual remaining cause of 115/519 residual errors after the first three fixes landed. Reached via lib/nutrition/food-resolver.ts's resolveFoodCandidateInner -> findRecipeCandidatesForPreparation, which runs getRecipes({ q: <full original query> }) whenever the current resolver finds ZERO catalog matches AND the query looks like a composite preparation (status PREPARATION_NEEDS_REVIEW). Long TBCA-derived names that aren't in the current resolver's catalog hit this path constantly in the 520-query dataset (roughly 22% of it).
callSitesFound.foundIn: isolated by bisecting resolveFoodCandidate's call graph after searchFoods alone (0 errors) failed to reproduce the residual 115 errors seen through the full resolveFoodCandidate/resolveFoodWithCanonicalShadow path

fix.approach: Shared minimal module lib/d1/like-safety.ts exporting capForLikePattern(text) (caps content to 40 chars, safe margin under the 50-char total-pattern limit) and MAX_LIKE_PATTERN_CONTENT_LENGTH. Applied ONLY to the fuzzy/contains LIKE branches in all four call sites above.
fix.preservedPrecision: Exact-match (=) and FTS (MATCH) branches in usda-foods.ts and canonical-food-search.ts keep the FULL, untruncated query text — capping only ever touches the already-fuzzy prefix/contains LIKE branches, so no semantically critical term is ever silently dropped from the paths that actually decide identity.
fix.noEscaping: listCustomFoods and getRecipes do not escape literal '%'/'_' from user input (documented, accepted trade-off: the worst case is a slightly more permissive match, never a crash or data leak). searchUsdaFoods normalizes input to [a-z0-9 ] before building any pattern, so it has no literal wildcard characters to worry about.

regressionTestsAdded: tests/like-pattern-hardening.test.ts (14 tests: capForLikePattern unit tests, LIKE/GLOB escaping behavior, listCustomFoods/searchUsdaFoods/getRecipes/canonical-food-search regression tests against the real 94-char TBCA name that reproduced the bug)
